props.title: Kuch Kuch Hota Hai

sections.content: Kuch Kuch Hota Hai (1998) revolutionized modern Bollywood romance, establishing Karan Johar's signature style of glossy production values, designer wardrobes, and emotionally charged triangular relationships. The film redefined college romance in Indian cinema, with Shah Rukh Khan and Kajol's chemistry setting a new benchmark that influenced countless films like Main Hoon Na (2004) and Student of the Year (2012). Rani Mukerji's brief but impactful role created the template for the sacrificial love interest that became a staple in films like Kal Ho Naa Ho (2003).

sections.content: The film's influence on fashion and style in Bollywood cannot be overstated. Kajol's short hair and athleisure looks as Anjali, and her later transformation into traditional wear created a cultural phenomenon. This styling technique of dramatic character transformation was later echoed in films like Kal Ho Naa Ho (2003) and Main Hoon Na (2004). The college portion's colorful sportswear and branded clothing established Karan Johar as Bollywood's style maven, influencing costume design for decades.

The film's soundtrack by Jatin-Lalit marked a turning point in Bollywood music, with "Tujhe Yaad Na Meri Aayee" and "Koi Mil Gaya" becoming cultural touchstones. The integration of western pop elements with traditional Indian melodies created a template followed by films like Mohabbatein (2000) and Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (2001). The film's use of the friendship-to-love trope influenced countless later works including Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na (2008). SUBHEAD: Legacy and Cultural Impact

movies.title: Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna
movies.slug: A complex drama about relationships and infidelity, challenging traditional Bollywood romance tropes

sections.content: The film's handling of grief, friendship, and parenthood created a new emotional depth in commercial Indian cinema. Little Anjali's role as a matchmaker between her father and her mother's best friend introduced a complexity to the traditional romance narrative that influenced films like Wake Up Sid (2009) and 2 States (2014). The movie's success also cemented Shah Rukh Khan's position as Bollywood's "King of Romance," a title that would define his career through films like Veer-Zaara (2004) and Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi (2008).
